seo.title: Trust center
seo.seo_description: Our verifiable commitments, what the software already allows and the list of documents we are preparing, with their status: everything you can ask us for.

translation.headline: Commitments. Proof you can ask for.
translation.subheadline: No big words here: what we commit to doing, what the software already allows, and the documents we are preparing so you can check it.

translation.title: Verifiable commitments.
translation.intro: Each one can be checked before and after go-live.

cards.title: You know where your data goes.
cards.text: Before any go-live, we hand over in writing the data-flow diagram: where data is stored, which external services are called, which backups exist.

cards.title: No external model without consent.
cards.text: No call to an external AI service is configured without your written agreement, and the system never switches to one without telling you.

cards.title: Your data stays yours.
cards.text: We do not reuse one customer's data for another customer or to train a model without that customer's specific authorization.

cards.title: You can leave.
cards.text: Your documents, configurations and workflows stay exportable; the contract provides for it.

cards.title: Decisions stay human.
cards.text: In the workflows we set up, any action that commits the business waits for a person's approval, unless you decide otherwise in writing.

cards.title: No claim without proof.
cards.text: We publish no testimonial, no figure and no certification that we cannot prove. When a capability is in pilot or planned, we write it.

blocks.role: Ce que le logiciel permet déjà, statuts disponibles.

translation.title: What the software already allows.
translation.intro: WorkStudio functions, verified on Nexora's test server. They support your process; they do not replace it.

cards.title: Roles and organizations.
cards.text: Who sees what, who can edit, by workspace.

cards.title: Audit log and caps.
cards.text: Administration actions are logged; consumption is capped by month.

cards.title: Single sign-on.
cards.text: Your teams sign in with your company account, at a common identity provider.

cards.title: Personal-information policy.
cards.text: Allow, mask or refuse sending personal information to a model outside the instance, by workspace.

cards.title: Traces and masking.
cards.text: Every model call is traced; names, emails and phone numbers can be masked in them.

cards.title: Each model's location and encrypted secrets.
cards.text: Each model shows where it runs; connector credentials are encrypted and kept on your instance.

blocks.role: Documents fournis sur demande, tous en préparation.

translation.title: Documents on request.
translation.intro: These are the documents we commit to providing. They are in preparation: none is available yet, and we will say so here as soon as one exists.

cards.title: The data-flow diagram for your installation.
cards.text: Where data is stored, which external services are called, which backups exist. The diagram template is yet to be written.

cards.title: The standard contract and data processing agreement.
cards.text: What Nexora does with the information you entrust to it, and what it refrains from doing.

cards.title: The list of subcontractors and locations.
cards.text: Who takes part in hosting and operations, and where.

cards.title: Proof of the hosting location in Quebec.
cards.text: Address, location clause, location of backups and logs, for the hosted mode.

cards.title: A privacy impact assessment template.
cards.text: To help your company document the assessment of an AI project.

cards.title: An incident procedure.
cards.text: Who assesses, who notifies, where the incident is recorded.

translation.title: Three planes of data.
translation.body: When we say “data”, we mean three different things. We treat them separately.

items.title: The site's public content.
items.text: What you read here: made to be published and indexed.

items.title: Your exchanges with Nexora.
items.text: Forms, emails, billing: they serve only to answer you and to serve you. The site's privacy policy, in preparation, will describe them.

items.title: Your system's data.
items.text: Your documents, conversations and databases: they stay inside the agreed perimeter, described by the data-flow diagram.

blocks.role: Ce que nous ne revendiquons pas.

cards.title: No customer named.
cards.text: We publish no customer name, no logo, no case study until we have the written agreement of the company concerned.

cards.title: No figure without measurement.
cards.text: Neither time saved, nor success rate, nor savings: they are measured at your site, during a pilot.

cards.title: No announced service level.
cards.text: Availability and response times are set out in the contract.

cards.title: No decreed compliance.
cards.text: A company's compliance depends on its practices, its contracts and its governance. No supplier confers it.

items.question: How do I ask for a document?
items.answer: Write to us through the contact form and name the document. While it is in preparation, we say so instead of promising you a date.

items.question: Do you have a security attestation?
items.answer: We claim none today. We describe what the software allows and what we document.

items.question: Who at Nexora can access my system?
items.answer: Only the access agreed in advance, described in the deployment study. In the on-premises mode, you grant it and can withdraw it.

items.question: Do you use an external model?
items.answer: Only if you accepted it in writing. It then appears on the data-flow diagram as an outbound flow.

translation.title: A proof is missing.
translation.text: Tell us which one. We will answer with what exists, what is in preparation and what we cannot yet state.
